name: Methane pyrolysis (turquoise hydrogen)
applications: hydrogen and ammonia with solid carbon co-product
principle: Methane is split into hydrogen and solid carbon without oxygen, using plasma, molten metal or salt, or a catalyst bed. No CO2 is formed in the reaction, and the carbon leaves as a solid such as carbon black that can be sold or stored. Monolith's plasma process runs at about 1650 °C.

process_steps.name: Pyrolysis reactor
equipment: plasma torch reactor, molten media reactor or catalytic bed

key_equipment: pyrolysis reactor (plasma, molten metal or catalytic)

source.note: Digital Refining / PTQ, Turquoise hydrogen production by methane pyrolysis, January 2022

reference_plants.name: Monolith Olive Creek 1, Nebraska
reference_plants.capacity: about 14,000 t/yr carbon black and about 2,500 t/yr hydrogen
reference_plants.status: commissioned 2020; Olive Creek 2 planned at about 194,000 t/yr carbon black and 40,000 t/yr hydrogen

source.note: Digital Refining / PTQ, Turquoise hydrogen production by methane pyrolysis, January 2022

reference_plants.name: BASF methane pyrolysis pilot, Ludwigshafen
reference_plants.status: under construction from 2019 per the article

source.note: Digital Refining / PTQ, Turquoise hydrogen production by methane pyrolysis, January 2022

advantages: No CO2 formed in the reaction, no CO2 storage needed
Solid carbon co-product with a market (carbon black)
limitations: Carbon co-product volume far exceeds the carbon black market at hydrogen scale
Needs more gas per kg of hydrogen than SMR

sources.note: Digital Refining / PTQ, Turquoise hydrogen production by methane pyrolysis, January 2022
